description:
# Claude Touches Grass 🌲🥾💻

Close the laptop—but don’t stop coding.
Join Coffee & Code Philadelphia for a hardcore outdoor coding session where developers, founders, researchers, and AI builders take Claude out of the terminal and onto the trail.
Bring your Apple Vision Pro, connect to Claude Code through remote control on your phone, or pack whatever portable setup lets you ship from the wilderness. We’ll hike, find a scenic place to set up, and spend focused time building together surrounded by actual trees instead of desktop wallpaper.
This is not a screen-free wellness retreat. There will be code.

### What to expect

* A social group hike with Philadelphia’s tech community
* Dedicated outdoor coding and building time
* Claude Code sessions controlled remotely from your phone
* Apple Vision Pro and other unconventional coding setups
* Conversations about AI, startups, open source, and whatever you’re building
* Optional food or coffee with the group afterward

Bring a project you want to advance, a difficult bug you want to defeat, or a completely unreasonable idea you want to prototype in the woods.
All hiking and coding experience levels are welcome. We’ll share the route, distance, difficulty, parking information, and weather updates before the event.

### What to bring

* A phone with Claude remote control configured
* Apple Vision Pro, laptop, tablet, or another portable setup
* A charged power bank
* Mobile hotspot or cellular data
* Comfortable hiking shoes
* Water and snacks
* Weather-appropriate clothing
* Sunscreen or bug spray as needed
* Your fully online, artificially hosted neural network

Friends are welcome—even the ones who don’t know what Claude is.
For everyone’s safety, save the immersive coding for our designated stops. Do not wear a Vision Pro or stare at your phone while actively hiking.
Come touch grass, summon Claude, and ship something in the wilderness. 🌿

name: (CS)²AI Online™ Seminar: Water Cybersecurity: Keeping It Pure
description:
In late July 2026, attackers reached into water and wastewater utilities in at least 12 US states. They exploited internet-exposed programmable logic controllers (PLCs), including Allen-Bradley MicroLogix 1100/1400, Schneider Modicon M340, and Siemens S7-1200 units. The attackers changed IP addresses and passwords to lock operators out of monitoring and control. In some cases they altered ladder logic in PLC project files. Utilities reported pressure loss and localized flooding, and operators had to fall back to manual operations. On July 30 the FBI and EPA issued a joint alert, and an Iran-linked group claimed responsibility.
The campaign follows a pattern that is years in the making. In 2023, CyberAv3ngers defaced Unitronics controllers at the Municipal Water Authority of Aliquippa. In 2024, American Water, the largest regulated U.S. water utility, was hit by a cyberattack, and Arkansas City switched to manual operations after an incident. In 2025, Poland reported ICS intrusions at five water treatment plants. The attack surface hasn't changed much in that time. It is still exposed PLCs and HMIs, default or shared credentials, integrator-managed remote access, and small utilities with few security staff.
The attackers and vulnerabilities in the core OT control system and SCADA technologies are not the only pieces of the puzzle that has created this perfect storm. The way that Water Utility OT systems have been designed, constructed, built, commissioned, and managed without cybersecurity oversight or involvement over the last several decades presents another unique problem in this critical infrastructure sector. System Integrators and Engineering firms who have been at the core of these processes are not trained and are not generally aware of the cybersecurity requirements that should have been incorporated into these systems, and the recent advisory from CISA reinforce this part of the problem:
FBI, CISA Warn of Third-Party ICS Integrator Risks:
https://securitytoday.com/articles/2026/09/28/fbi-cisa-warn-of-third-party-ics-integrator-risks.aspx
Lastly, we will wrap the session with recent cybersecurity regulations in Water-adjacent sectors that hint that this may be brought into the Water Utility sector in the near future
This session looks at the following geo-political, technical, and sector-specific issues and ends with a case study for a practical 3-step process that has been proven to solve this issue with over a dozen successful implementations in the water/waste water industry:
1\. Geo\-political and Financial Gain motivations for why the US Water Utility Industry is being targeted
2\. Technical vulnerabilities that have allowed the attacks to work: How attackers find and take over exposed controllers and what the attacks do at the logic and network layers
3\. Unique challenges that have arisen over decades of not having cybersecurity\-in\-the\-loop as Water Utility OT Systems are designed\, constructed\, built\, commissioned\, and managed \(Systems Integrators and Engineering Firms lacking core cybersecurity knowledge and awareness
4\. What the sector needs moving forward \> How do we fix this?
⁃ Which defensive measures work: removing direct internet exposure, segmenting control networks behind secure gateways, strict access control lists, locking PLCs against unauthorized logic changes with key switches, verifying project file integrity, monitoring for configuration changes, and keeping manual operation ready
⁃ Review of a case study for how these challenges are being resolved with a practical and proven 3-step process >> Assess, Remediate, and Monitor/Manage
5\. How the federal response and the push for water\-sector security standards may shape utility obligations in the months ahead\.

# ☕ The OG Coffee&Code Meetup

### A Blockspace Community × Coffee&Code Collaboration

Before the hype. Before the buzzwords. Before “AI-powered everything.”
This is **The OG Coffee&Code**—the meetup that started it all, now presented in collaboration with the **Blockspace Community**.
No panels. No pitches. No pressure.
Just good people, good coffee, and focused time to build, learn, and connect.

## What this meetup is

An open, welcoming space for coders, builders, designers, and curious minds.
Bring your own project, homework, startup, side quest, experiment, or idea. Work at your own pace, meet other builders, ask questions, exchange ideas, or simply enjoy being productive around like-minded people.
Expect:

* Focused building time
* Organic conversations
* Spontaneous debugging
* Knowledge sharing
* Genuine community

This meetup is beginner-friendly, expert-respected, and ego-free.

## What this meetup is not

❌ A lecture
❌ A sales event
❌ A recruiting trap
❌ A 90-minute presentation

## How it works

1. Show up
2. Grab coffee ☕
3. Open your laptop, notebook, or sketchpad
4. Work at your own pace
5. Chat when you want and focus when you need
6. Leave having made progress—or at least a new friend

## Who should attend

* Software engineers and data professionals
* Students and self-learners
* Founders and indie hackers
* Designers, tinkerers, and technologists
* Members of the Blockspace and Coffee&Code communities
* Anyone who enjoys building things with other humans

Whether this is your first Coffee&Code, you are part of the Blockspace Community, or you have been attending since day one, you are welcome.
This collaboration brings together two communities around a shared goal: creating a relaxed, supportive space where people can build, learn, and connect.

**Come for the code.**
**Stay for the community.**
**Leave caffeinated. ☕🚀**

name: Hiring Talent and Getting Hired in an AI-Driven Market
description:
Join fellow ProductTank members and a panel of career and recruiting experts from Computer Enterprises, Inc. for a conversation about how AI is reshaping the hiring process from both sides of the table.

Whether you’re a hiring manager trying to understand how the candidate experience and talent landscape are changing, a product professional navigating your own career, or simply curious about how AI is influencing recruiting and hiring, you’ll come away with new perspectives and practical takeaways.

***Some of the areas we’ll explore:***

* How AI is changing the job search and candidate hunt
* Using AI for resumes, LinkedIn profiles, and interview preparation
* What recruiters are paying attention to
* How hiring managers might evolve their hiring process
* How candidates can stand out in a crowded market
* What AI can help with and where human judgment still matters
* Common misconceptions about recruiting and AI
* How recruiters are using AI today, including some of CEI’s experiences and lessons learned

***Event Info:***

* **When:** Wednesday, October 7th, 2026
* **Time:** 6:00-8:30 PM ET
* **Location:** CEI Plymouth Meeting Office
* **Address:** **[660 W Germantown Pike](https://www.google.com/maps/search/660+W+Germantown+Pike?entry=gmail&source=g),** Suite LL100, Plymouth Meeting, PA 19462

***Event Schedule:***

* **6:00–6:30 PM:** Networking
* **6:30–7:30 PM:** Panel discussion and Q&A
* **7:30–8:30 PM:** Networking and farewell

***About Our Partner & Sponsor****:*
CEI is an AI platform engineering firm that helps organizations build and scale digital products, modernize technology platforms, and unlock value from data and AI. We partner with enterprise teams across product, engineering, data, and technology to accelerate innovation, improve delivery, and bring new capabilities to market faster. In addition to our engineering and consulting services, CEI helps organizations attract, hire, and retain top technology talent through specialized recruiting and workforce solutions. By combining technology expertise with talent solutions, CEI helps organizations move from strategy to execution and achieve measurable business outcomes.

***About Our Panelists:***
Our ProductTank Organizer Joshua Aversa will moderate the conversation between:

* **Matthew Linneman**
*VP, Key Accounts & Recruiting, CEI*
Matthew Linneman is Vice President of Key Accounts & Recruiting at CEI, where he has spent more than 16 years helping organizations build high-performing technology teams and scale strategic client partnerships. Throughout his tenure, he has held leadership roles spanning sales, staffing, recruiting, and business development, and today leads CEI’s recruiting and key account organizations with a focus on talent strategy, growth, and innovation.

* **Matthew Pribbernow**
*Senior Team Lead, CEI*
Matthew Pribbernow is a Senior Team Lead at CEI with nearly 10 years of experience helping organizations attract, hire, and retain top technology talent. He leads recruiting initiatives across a wide range of technical disciplines and partners closely with both hiring leaders and candidates to build teams that support innovation and business growth.

* **Katie Dougherty**
*Senior Professional Recruiter, CEI*
Katie Dougherty is a Senior Professional Recruiter at CEI with more than five years of experience helping technology professionals connect with opportunities that align with their skills and career goals. She works closely with both candidates and hiring managers and brings firsthand insight into today’s evolving technology job market, hiring trends, and candidate expectations.

We hope you’ll join us for a practical and candid conversation about navigating the increasingly AI-influenced product talent market!

name: Better Data for AI is Everyone's Job
description:
**PLEASE REGISTER ON THE DAMA PHILADELPHIA [WEBSITE](https://damaphila.starchapter.com/meetinginfo.php?id=51&ts=1790867055) TO RECEIVE THE CORRECT ZOOM LINK FOR THE EVENT**

**11am-12pm EST:** **Terri Mikol -** Data & Analytics Governance Advisor.
Better Data is Everyone's Job
Organizations know they need data governance for analytics and AI, but often lack the time, budget, or resources to launch another major program. This session presents a practical approach that uses the organization's existing people, skills, processes, and technology to improve data quality, clarify ownership, increase data literacy, and build sustainable governance without a large investment.
**12pm-12:30pm EST:** **Marilu Lopez** the owner and CEO of SEGDA company
Most organizations face pressure to extract value from their data. They often jump straight into implementing MDM initiatives, moving to the cloud, adopting advanced analytics, and now, integrating AI, without a solid understanding of the problems they need to solve or the priorities involved. However, there is a growing awareness of the importance of managing data more effectively, even though the path to achieving this remains unclear. A Data Strategy is essential for setting priorities and guiding resource allocation effectively. This session explains how to develop Data Strategies using the PAC (Pragmatic, Agile, and Communicable) Data Strategy Method.
Create your Data Strategies with the right stakeholders in a pragmatic, agile way, and communicate them effectively using a Canvas.
**12:30 - 1:15pm EST:** **Swati Prasad** \- Senior Manager\, Enterprise Data Governance — American Express\. Founder\, DataTrustHub \| Creator\, DataPolis\.
Policy as Code, Compliance as a Token
Swati Prasad serves as Senior Manager of Enterprise Data Governance at American Express, where she leads initiatives focused on data quality, risk controls, and regulatory compliance frameworks. She is the founder and primary contributor to DataTrustHub, an online publication exploring real-world data governance, and creator of DataPolis, a storytelling series designed to make DAMA-DMBOK2 standards accessible across organizations. Her recent research work focuses on integrating smart contracts, pre-chain validation, and distributed ledger technologies to eliminate manual control vulnerabilities and establish authoritative single sources of truth for enterprise analytics and AI.
Data governance depends on custodians who verify where data came from and whether it followed policy. Today that verification happens after the fact, from metadata attached to the data set, which makes audits slow and leaves compliance failures to be found late.
This talk proposes moving verification into the data lifecycle itself. At each stage, a smart contract confirms that the relevant organizational policy was followed and issues a token as proof. The contract relies on an oracle, and the right oracle depends on how subjective the policy is: software code for objective rules, a decentralized committee for judgment calls, or a gatekeeper where accountability must rest with a named party. The final certification checks the full chain of tokens and attests to the compliance of the data. Because each token acts as a micro compliance record that is decentralized and independently verifiable, regulators can audit the record directly instead of relying on the custodian's account of it. The core argument is that policy written as code, paired with oracles matched to the policy, shifts governance from retrospective inspection to continuous proof, and makes the choice of oracle the central governance decision.

name: RSVP to the next Philly RHUG!
description:
**REGISTER HERE: [https://reg.experiences.redhat.com/flow/redhat/4900050/rhexpressregistration/page/expressregistration?sc_cid=RHCTN1260000495451](https://reg.experiences.redhat.com/flow/redhat/4900050/rhexpressregistration/page/expressregistration?sc_cid=RHCTN1260000495451)**

In recent months, AI has fundamentally reshaped cybersecurity. Automated tooling now discovers open-source vulnerabilities and generates exploits at unprecedented speeds. As the sheer volume and velocity of CVE disclosures overwhelm traditional workflows, IT and security teams face a daunting challenge: How do you patch rapidly without destabilizing mission-critical production environments?
Join us for the next [Philadelphia Red Hat User Group (RHUG)](https://reg.experiences.redhat.com/flow/redhat/4900050/rhexpressregistration/page/expressregistration?sc_cid=RHCTN1260000495451) to explore how Red Hat turns the tide on AI-driven threats by securing the software supply chain from code to deployment.
What we'll cover:

* Red Hat Trusted Libraries: How cryptographically signed, SLSA-compliant binaries neutralize upstream risks before code hits production.

name: PLUG Central - Jitsi Meet: 7-9PM; Speaker from 7:30-8:30PM
description:
Please join us for PLUG Central. During the pandemic we meet on-line at Jitsi Meet, beginning at 7pm. RSVPs are optional. Anyone interested in Linux and Free and Open Source software is welcome to attend. We welcome all levels of expertise, whether you're just curious, a hobbyist, or a professional.

Jitsi Meet agenda:

Q&A with emcee CJ Fearnley from 7-7:30PM. Bring your Linux (and related) questions for a group exploration.

The main presentation from 7:30-8:30PM: TBD.

Q&A continued from 8:30-9PM.

After the pandemic dissipates, we plan to again meet in Lecture Hall A in Griffith Hall at USP in Philadelphia. We plan to revert to the original speaker slot from 8-9PM with Q&A at the beginning to better support travel constraints.

After the presentation some of us adjourn to Clarkville (http://www.clarkvillephilly.com/) a nearby pizza and craft beer restaurant.

University of the Sciences in Philadelphia (USP)
Griffith Hall (Room "A" or "C", look for the signs)
600 South 43rd Street
Philadelphia, PA 19104-4495

USP is located in University City. Driving directions are available at http://www.phillylinux.org/locations/usp.html, or http://www.usip.edu/directions, both of which have an aerial view of the campus buildings. USP is also easily accessible by public transportation.

Often, the door to Griffith Hall is locked at 7PM. If you find the door locked, please contact the security guard (usually in the booth in the parking lot) and tell them that the monthly PLUG (Philadelphia Linux User Group) meeting in Griffith Hall is tonight. If there is no one in the booth you can call UCS's public safety number at 215.895.1117 and they will radio personnel to unlock the door. Our sponsor is Zhiwei Liu in the Chemistry department. Security knows this and will almost always open the door for you and have it unlocked so other participants can enter without issue.
